resources.string: What you type stays on this device. The only network use is GIF search, and only when you open it.
Turn on KeyHack in your keyboard settings. Android warns that any keyboard can collect what you type; KeyHack never sends your typing anywhere.
Import your own images; they become WhatsApp-style stickers (512×512 WebP). Any emoji can also be sent as a sticker from the keyboard\'s 🖼 button. Images stay on this device.
%1$d stickers added, %2$d images could not be read

Switch any time with the DEV button on the keyboard bar. Advanced adds the dev row (Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, arrows), code symbols on the top row and the PC layout. Terminal apps always open in advanced mode.
Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt and arrows above the keyboard
Space-separated: esc tab ctrl alt meta left right up down home end pgup pgdn ins fdel f1…f12, or any character
Fixes typos and accents (nao → não) on space. Backspace undoes it.
Counts words you use, on this device only. Never in password fields.
Open in PC mode for these apps
Package names, separated by commas. Toggle PC mode anywhere with the PC button on the toolbar.

PC mode is a full Hacker\'s Keyboard layout: Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, Meta, arrows and an Fn layer with F1–F12, Home/End, PgUp/PgDn. Tap Ctrl/Alt once for the next key, twice to lock. Keys are sent as real key events, so Ctrl+C works in Termux and SSH.
Off = KeyHack never uses the network
GIFs use your own Giphy API key. A free test key (limited searches per hour) is at developers.giphy.com; production keys may be paid. It is stored only on this device.
Only what you type in the GIF search box is sent, over HTTPS, to the provider you chose. The provider also sees your API key and IP address.

No analytics, no crash reporting, no telemetry. Learned words are stored in a private file that is never backed up. Typing in password fields and in apps that ask for no personalized learning is never learned. Use the 🕶 button on the toolbar for incognito typing.

• DEV on the keyboard bar switches between the simple keyboard (chat) and the advanced one (Ctrl, Alt, arrows, terminal).
• Swipe up on a key to type the symbol in its corner (@ _ / " and more; in advanced mode also { } [ ]); long-press for accents.
• ?123 has every code symbol on one page.
• Slide on the space bar to move the cursor.
• Long-press space to switch keyboards; long-press comma for settings.
• Toolbar: ☺ emoji, GIF, </> dev tools (case, Base64, JSON, hashes, UUID…), PC mode, 🕶 incognito.
